question.leadin: In order to crack this German code, Polish and British cryptographers designed mechanical devices called "bombes" [bombs].
question.text: Name this supposedly unbreakable code that was finally cracked by codebreakers at Bletchley Park.
question.clue: This device was combated by the bombe, a form of early computer.

swap.text: Tycho Brahe ("TY-co BRAH-hay") was a successor of Copernicus. Although he died when his bladder burst on a carriage ride, his data helped this man formulate his three laws of planetary motion.
swap.clue: In 1615, this scientist defended his mother for 6 years in a witchcraft trial. This astronomer had earlier defied Church doctrine by claiming that the planets move in ellipses, not circles, as the first in his three laws of planetary motion.

question.text: This Prussian leader and victor at Laon defeated Napoleon at Leipzig. He crushed Marmont's Sixth Corps and was promoted to Field Marshall after the battle.
question.clue: Dismissed from his governorship of Pomerania in 1812 for his ardent support of another war, at Auerstadt, he repeatedly led unsuccessful cavalry charges, and refused to surrender with the rest of Hohenlohe's corps.

swap.leadin: This city's Burgerbraukeller was the site of an uprising on November 8th, 1923 supported by Erich Ludendorff.
swap.text: Name this Bavarian city, the site of Adolf Hitler's failed Beer Hall Putsch.
swap.clue: That used in Rollerball is the BMW Headquarters and Museum.

question.text: Swiss banks notoriously stored gold from the plunder of this government's occupied territories. The Bergier Commission investigated Switzerland's involvement in the auctions of "degenerate art" rebuked by this government.
question.answerHtml: Nazi Germany [or the Third Reich; prompt on Germany; prompt on the Reich]
question.clue: This country assigned its best fighter pilots to JV 44 to fly the first jet-powered fighter, the Messerschmitt 262.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some secret police agencies.
swap.text: This agency was the secret police of East Germany. Under the direction of Markus Wolf, this agency instituted physiological destruction tactics known as Zersetzung.
swap.answerHtml: Stasi [or the Ministry of State Security; or Ministerium fur Staatsicherheit; or MfS]
swap.clue: This organization installed X-Ray machines in prisons, which were used to give Lukemia to political prisoners.

question.leadin: This politician authored a report that defined 30 degrees North as the dividing line between the "prosperous North" and "developing South."
question.text: Name this man who also served as Governing Mayor of Berlin during the construction of the Berlin Wall. He was succeeded by Helmut Schmidt after an aide of his was revealed to be a spy.
question.clue: During one diplomatic trip, this man made the shocking gesture of kneeling before a memorial to the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, and he was criticized by some for agreeing to put an eastern border at the Oder-Neisse Line.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Germany's role in World War I.
swap.text: This decades-old grand strategy involved sweeping into France through Belgium on the event of a two-front war with France and Russia. Its breakdown under Moltke's command at the Marne led to trench warfare.
swap.clue: This German strategy, named for a former German field marshal, advocated sweeping through France, then transporting troops east to handle the slower-to-mobilize Russian forces.

question.leadin: This war began following the declaration of the Twelve Articles by the Swabian League.
question.text: Name this war, in which Thomas Muntzer led one side to defeat at the 1525 Battle of Frankenhausen.
question.answerHtml: German Peasants' War [or German Peasants' Revolt; or Deutscher Baumkrieg]
question.clue: During this conflict, Sebastian Lotzer drafted resolutions calling for economic and religious liberty, called the Twelve Articles.

swap.text: The Hohenstaufens themselves originated from this southwestern region of today's Germany, which lies in the present day state of Baden-Wurttemberg.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this region attempted to invade Italy but was stymied by Otto I, who secured the crowns of Lombardy and this region.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a school.
question.text: Established in 1919, this school of design moved to in 1926, and closed because of Nazi hostility in 1933.

swap.leadin: A tremendous galleon known as the Adler, or "Eagle," of this city was ignobly repurposed for undertaking trade missions to Spain after not being sent on military campaigns against Sweden.
swap.text: Name this "Free City." This "Queen" of a certain medieval organization was considered one of the "Five Glories" of the Holy Roman Empire, along with Florence, Rome, Pisa, and Venice.
swap.answerHtml: Lübeck [accept the Free City of Lübeck; accept the Adler von Lübeck or the Eagle of Lübeck]
swap.clue: Adolf II ceded this city to Henry the Lion after building it on land conquered from the Obotrites.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of printed books.
question.text: Everyone loves this inventor of the movable type printing press, who printed a namesake version of the bible from his workshop in Mainz.
question.clue: This man's invention of hand molds and an oil-based substance helped him create his most well-known invention.

swap.text: Lloyd George delivered the Mansion House Speech in response to this international incident, in which the German boat Panther drove up to the namesake African town to say "Hello," as the French made moves to annex Morocco.
swap.clue: Before becoming Prime Minister, Lloyd George gave the Mansion House speech in response to this 1911 crisis in which Germany sent the gunboat Panther to the namesake Moroccan port. Lloyd George argued in his speech that Britain would pursue honor over peace.

question.leadin: Name these powerful women in 19th-century Europe.
question.text: This mistress of King Ludwig of Bavaria sought to limit the power of the Jesuits and ultramontanists, but fell from grace in the student revolutions of 1848.
question.answerHtml: Lola Montez [accept either underlined name; or Marie Dolores Eliza Rosanna Gilbert]
question.clue: The final completed film of Max Ophuls shows her played by Martine Carol, opposite the Circus Master played by Peter Ustinov.

swap.leadin: Though he devised the strategy of encirclement that won this battle, Max Hoffman was largely ignored by the contemporary press.
swap.text: Name this crushing German victory of World War I in which 92,000 Russian troops were captured in East Prussia. This battle's victors named it as vengeance for a Teutonic defeat that had occurred 500 years prior.
swap.answerHtml: Second Battle of Tannenberg [or Battle of Tannenberg; do not accept “First Battle of Tannenberg” or “Battle of Grunwald”]
swap.clue: Rather than report defeat at this battle to Nicholas II, the losing commander, Alexander Samsonov, decided to kill himself.

question.leadin: These people established a capital at Arkona after an expedition demolished their temple at Rethra.
question.text: Name these people once led by the chief Niklot, whose son also led an uprising of these people but was smashed at the Battle of Verchen, after which he founded the monastery at Doberan.
question.answerHtml: Wends [or Wendish; or Obotrites;or Winedas; or Vindr; or Wenden; or Vender; or Wendowie; prompt on Slavs]
question.clue: Following Otto II's defeat at the Battle of Stilo in Calabria, the Obotrites under Mstivoj launched a 986 uprising against the Empire aimed at overthrowing the imperial 'marks' in the territory of these people, who are also called the Lutici.

swap.leadin: A community of "radical" members of this movement known as the Skevikare toured Northern Europe in exile for eleven years before settling on an island off the coast of Stockholm.
swap.text: Name this reform movement heralded by Philipp Jakob Spener and August Hermann Francke, which broke from the Lutheran emphasis on doctrine and theology and instead stressed personal faith.
swap.clue: The Soter movement accused the Zoe Movement of resembling this Lutheran reform movement, which stressed individual knowledge of the Bible. This movement was led by Philipp Spener.

question.text: This German commander wiped out the Hereros as commander in chief of German South West Africa, by cornering them into the Kalahari Desert, and poisoning their water Kefka-style.
question.answerHtml: Lothar von Trotha (Adrian Dietrich Lothar von Trotha)
question.clue: The Herero Genocide was largely the handiwork of this German commander, who drove the Herero into the desert after the Battle of Waterberg, poisoned their water, and encircled the desert with his soldiers so that they could not escape.

swap.leadin: This polity came under the rule of the Franconian Hohenzollerns in 1415, after which it eventually came to dominate the Duchy of Prussia.
swap.text: Name this polity corresponding to a modern German state surrounding Berlin. It lends its name to a famous neoclassical Gate in that city.
swap.answerHtml: Margraviate of Brandenburg [Also accept March of Brandenburg or Electorate of Brandenburg.]
swap.clue: The portion of this polity east of the Oder-Neisse line is the Neumark, which was transferred to Poland following World War II.
